subject: Unexpected mid-month overage: tokenizer change impact on usage
messages:
From: Sam Wong <sam.wong@altaranalytics.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc: accounts@altaranalytics.com
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected mid-month overage — large spike starting Sep 1

Hi Markus,

We noticed a sudden ~4.8x increase in token consumption starting Sep 1 on our production calls to the streaming generation endpoint (same prompts, same traffic). Our internal engineering team traced the root cause to a tokenizer update on our side (we pushed a library update that changed whitespace handling) but the token counts shown on the invoice look like they reflect the post-change tokenization for the full month, not the traffic split.

Attached is a small sample of requests (altar_overage_sample_requests.txt) showing the before/after text and our token counts. Can you:
- Confirm how Redwood attributes tokens when a customer-side tokenizer changes mid-billing-cycle
- Provide an export of token counts for the sample session IDs in the attached file
- Temporarily hold the mid-cycle invoice while we reconcile?

This overage is material for our month and we need to resolve before payment is processed. If you need anything else (sample timestamps or session ids), Sam and our finance alias are on this thread.

Thanks,
Sam Wong
Head of Platform Engineering
Altar Analytics
From: markus.klein@redwood.ai
To: Sam Wong <sam.wong@altaranalytics.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 11:04:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-month overage — large spike starting Sep 1

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear samples. I copied Ben from billing and Kimberly from operations so we can get a token export and make a proposal for remediation. Planned next steps from our side: 

1) Ben will pull a token-count export for the session IDs/timestamp window you provided and include per-request attribution.
2) Kimberly will check routing & model-variant logs to ensure there was no server-side model or tokenizer change on Redwood's end.
3) We'll propose either a one-time retroactive adjustment (credit) for the re-tokenized volume or provide the raw evidence if it matches our metering rules.

We can place the invoice on provisional hold for up to 14 days while we finish the audit. Please confirm you want a hold and whether Altar prefers a credit or invoice-side adjustment if we agree it was caused by your tokenizer change.

I expect a preliminary export from Ben by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Sam Wong <sam.wong@altaranalytics.com>
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 10:28:55 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-month overage — tokenization window export attached

Hi Sam,

Attached is a preliminary token export for the windows you requested (token_export_sample_window.csv). Quick summary of what we found after matching your session IDs and timestamps:

- For the sample 2026-09-01 02:03 UTC request set, Redwood recorded 4.79x more input tokens compared to the historical baseline for the same prompt text (we included the raw prompt in the CSV).
- The increase correlates precisely with the timestamps you flagged and there are no server-side tokenizer changes or model switches on Redwood for your account during that window — Kimberly confirmed no deployment changes.
- Our metering uses the model-side tokenization at the time of request; that is, tokens are counted post-tokenizer at generation time. If a customer changes their pre-processing and that increases token volume, the usage is charged accordingly per our usage policy.

Given the clear customer-side tokenizer delta, our usual path is to offer a one-time goodwill credit for the unexpected spike when the customer provides: (a) a short explanation and (b) confirmation of the rollforward that caused the re-tokenization. We can issue a credit memo equal to the delta tokens for Sep 1–Sep 3 sample window and then extrapolate if you confirm the change was global for all traffic.

Options for Altar
- Option A (recommended): Apply a one-time credit for the observed delta for the full impacted window. We will create a credit memo and adjust the mid-cycle invoice; total credit will be itemized on the adjusted invoice.
- Option B: Keep invoice as-is, but we provide the full per-request export and sample evidence for your internal accounting to make a case for your own adjustments.

If you want Option A, reply with the language you need for internal approvals and we will prepare a credit memo (I can provisionally apply the hold you requested until we finalize).

Attachments: token_export_sample_window.csv (export stub, columns: timestamp, request_id, prompt_excerpt, tokens_recorded)

Regards,
Ben Carter
Billing Operations Lead
Redwood Inference
From: Sam Wong <sam.wong@altaranalytics.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc: accounts@altaranalytics.com
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-month overage — tokenization window export attached

Thanks Ben — that export is exactly what we needed.

Altar accepts Option A. Our finance team asks for a brief memo line that states: "One-time billing credit applied due to customer-side tokenizer change that materially increased measured token usage; credit amount corresponds to the delta tokens recorded between 2026-09-01 and 2026-09-03 for affected requests." 

Please go ahead and: 
- Apply the provisional hold (we won't remit payment for the disputed line until the adjusted invoice is issued)
- Generate the credit memo and adjusted invoice and send a PDF to accounts@altaranalytics.com
- Include the per-request CSV as backup on the adjusted invoice package

We'll sign any short MOU language if needed; attaching the signed confirmation in the thread once we have it.

Thanks again for the quick turnaround.

Sam Wong
Head of Platform Engineering
Altar Analytics
